very time we carry out a chemical reaction— from fundamental research stud- ies to practical industrial applications— the yield of the reaction is extremely important. Did we obtain all the product we could expect? Chapter 2 shows how to calculate the amount of product expected when we start a reaction with particu- lar amounts of the reactants. This calculation assumes that the reaction goes to completion— that is, all of the limiting reagent is consumed. The resulting number, called the theoretical yield, repre sents the maximum amount of product that could be obtained from that reaction.
